blocks.content: Understanding Manipur's three principal ethnic-community groupings — Meitei, Naga, and Kuki-Zo — is essential not only for standard demography questions but for understanding the state's contemporary political situation (Chapter 12). This chapter presents the factual, historical-anthropological picture of each community neutrally and separately from the sensitive current-affairs discussion in Chapter 12.

cells: approx 40% — concentrated overwhelmingly in the hill districts
approx 985 females per 1,000 males — among the more favourable sex ratios of Indian states

blocks.content: Manipur's population is broadly composed of three principal ethnic-linguistic community groupings, each with distinct historical, cultural, religious and geographic characteristics — understanding these as factually distinct (while recognising each contains further internal diversity of sub-groups) is foundational to Manipur's demography chapter.

cells: Manipur's largest single ethnic community; predominantly Hindu (Vaishnavite, following the 18th-century conversion, Chapter 2) with a significant Sanamahi (indigenous faith) minority; not currently classified as a Scheduled Tribe; the Meitei Pangal (Manipuri Muslims) are a historically and culturally distinct Meitei-language-speaking Muslim community, also based mainly in the valley

Part of the wider Naga ethnic-linguistic family also found in neighbouring Nagaland; recognised as Scheduled Tribes; predominantly Christian; includes sub-groups such as Tangkhul, Mao, Maram, Poumai, Zeliangrong and others, each with distinct traditions

Part of the wider Kuki-Chin-Mizo (Zo) ethnic-linguistic family also found in Mizoram, parts of Nagaland, Assam and Myanmar; recognised as Scheduled Tribes; predominantly Christian; includes numerous sub-tribes historically classified under both 'Kuki' and, more recently, an increasingly used 'Zo' or 'Kuki-Zo' collective identity term

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Meitei = valley, predominantly Hindu/Sanamahi, NOT currently a Scheduled Tribe. Naga and Kuki-Zo = hills, predominantly Christian, ARE Scheduled Tribes. This valley/hills-cum-religion-cum-ST-status matrix is the single most important demographic framework for understanding virtually everything else in Manipur's contemporary polity chapters.

items: Meitei (Manipuri) is the official language of the state and the majority language of the Imphal Valley, belonging to the Tibeto-Burman language family; it has its own indigenous script, the Meitei Mayek, which fell out of common use for a long period (following the 18th-century adoption of Bengali-script conventions, Chapter 2) but has since been actively revived and is now taught in schools and used in official contexts alongside Bengali-derived script.
Meitei (Manipuri) is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, reflecting its status as a nationally recognised major language.

Naga and Kuki-Zo hill communities speak numerous distinct Tibeto-Burman languages/dialects specific to each sub-tribe, with English and Hindi also widely used, particularly in education (given the historical influence of Christian missionary education in the hill districts) and administration.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Meitei Mayek is the indigenous Meitei script (distinct from the Bengali-derived script adopted after 18th-century Hindu conversion) — its modern revival and current use in schools is a frequently tested language-policy fact.

items: Population (2011): approx 28.56 lakh; ST share approx 40% (concentrated in the hills); very small SC share (~2-3%).
Meitei = Imphal Valley, predominantly Hindu/Sanamahi, not currently a Scheduled Tribe; Meitei Pangal = Manipuri Muslim community.
Naga and Kuki-Zo = hill districts, Scheduled Tribes, predominantly Christian; each is an umbrella term for multiple sub-tribes.
Meitei (Manipuri) language: Tibeto-Burman family, official state language, included in the Constitution's Eighth Schedule; written in the revived indigenous Meitei Mayek script.
